summary: First edition. A Fairhope domestic strangulation arrest, the Spanish Fort bowling alley shooting arrest, child sexual abuse charges in Elberta and Foley, and three federal sentences for Baldwin County men.

entries.title: Domestic strangulation arrest, Fairhope: Lito Aquiriano Romero
body: Lito Aquiriano Romero, 44, was arrested by Fairhope police at 2:04 a.m. Monday and booked into the county jail on charges of domestic violence by strangulation, which covers choking or suffocating a family or household member, and coercion.
He was still in custody when the roster was read Monday afternoon.

entries.title: Spanish Fort bowling alley shooting: Gregory McDonald
body: Spanish Fort police say Gregory McDonald, 22, of Semmes, and Jamarcus Grayson, 24, of Mobile, fought inside Eastern Shore Lanes on Eastern Shore Boulevard late on Oct. 3. Police say a gun fell from Grayson, who picked it up and ran outside; McDonald chased him and fired several shots, striking two empty cars, and Grayson fired back and hit McDonald once.

McDonald was arrested Oct. 21 and booked on two counts of shooting into an unoccupied building and one of reckless endangerment; police describe the targets as cars and also cited a probation violation. The jail roster shows him released. Police said Grayson acted in self-defense but was carrying a gun while under indictment; he was arrested Oct. 14 on a charge of being a person forbidden to carry a weapon and is held without bond.

entries.title: Child sexual abuse material charges, Elberta: Timothy Eyres
body: The Baldwin County Sheriff's Office says it began investigating the online activity of Timothy Eyres, 66, of Elberta, on Sept. 22, and searched his electronic device under warrant on Oct. 15. The sheriff's office says the device held material depicting the sexual abuse of children.

Eyres faces four counts of possession of child sexual abuse material under Code of Alabama 13A-12-192(b). The sheriff's office says his bond is $100,000 cash, with release conditions of no contact with children, no internet, no guns and GPS monitoring. He was in custody on Oct. 26.

entries.title: Child sex abuse arrest, Foley: Collin James Nelson
body: Foley police say detectives arrested Collin James Nelson, 29, of Foley, on Tuesday, Oct. 21, the day after a report was made. He was booked on a charge of sexual abuse of a child under 12 and was in custody on Oct. 26.

entries.title: Fairhope meth case: Joseph Chase Gatlin and Jason Stephen Nelson
body: Fairhope police arrested two men at the same time and place on Monday morning, Oct. 20, under one case number, at a highway and county-road intersection the city's log does not name.

Joseph Chase Gatlin, 42, was booked into the county jail on charges of selling or distributing methamphetamine and tampering with physical evidence; Fairhope lists the charge as possession with intent to distribute. He was in custody on Oct. 26. Jason Stephen Nelson, 52, was booked on methamphetamine possession and drug paraphernalia and has been released.

entries.title: Domestic strangulation arrest: Jerry Louis Brown Jr.
body: Jerry Louis Brown Jr., 43, was arrested by sheriff's deputies late Friday, Oct. 23, and booked on charges of domestic violence by strangulation, second-degree domestic violence and two counts of harassment of a family member. He was in custody on Oct. 26.

entries.title: Sexual abuse arrest: Germaine Charles Williams
body: Germaine Charles Williams, 50, was arrested by sheriff's deputies on Oct. 21 and booked on charges of first-degree sexual abuse and third-degree assault. He was in custody on Oct. 26.

entries.title: Rape arrest: Stephen Allen White
body: Stephen Allen White, 48, was arrested by sheriff's deputies on Oct. 20 and booked on a rape charge, listed on the roster as "Rape-Strong Arm," and a harassment charge. The roster shows him released.

entries.title: Aggravated assault arrest, Daphne: Tara Christin O'Rourke
body: Tara Christin O'Rourke, 46, was arrested by Daphne police shortly after midnight on Oct. 20 and booked on charges of aggravated assault with a weapon and harassment of a family member. The roster shows her released. Daphne's public arrest log for the week does not list this arrest.

entries.title: Residential burglary arrest: Scott Curry Graham
body: Scott Curry Graham, 42, was arrested by sheriff's deputies late on Oct. 23 and booked on a charge of burglary of a residence by force. He was in custody on Oct. 26.

entries.title: Drug trafficking arrest: Telsa Nicole Delatorre
body: Telsa Nicole Delatorre, 34, was arrested by sheriff's deputies on Oct. 22 and booked on a drug trafficking charge and a probation revocation. She was in custody on Oct. 26.

entries.title: Stolen property, drugs and jail contraband: Fouad Magdy Marcos
body: Fouad Magdy Marcos, 46, was booked into the county jail on Oct. 24 on charges of buying or receiving stolen property, three counts of possessing dangerous drugs, and promoting prison contraband (drugs), which covers bringing drugs into a jail. The roster gives an arrest time of 9:05 a.m. on Oct. 26, two days after the booking date. He was in custody on Oct. 26.

entries.title: DUI and marijuana distribution, Gulf Shores: William Charles Bateman
body: William Charles Bateman, 34, was arrested by Gulf Shores police on Sunday afternoon, Oct. 25, and booked on charges of DUI (combined substances), selling or distributing marijuana, possessing a synthetic narcotic, second-degree marijuana possession and second-offense drug paraphernalia. The roster shows him released.

entries.title: Unsolved: man shot behind Foley bar
body: The sheriff's office says a 35-year-old man drove himself to Baldwin Health around 3 a.m. on Oct. 18 with several gunshot wounds and was flown to Sacred Heart Hospital in Pensacola. He could not identify who shot him, the sheriff's office says, and said only that it happened in Foley.

Foley officers helped find a scene in the rear parking lot of Good Time Charley's off Highway 98. Surveillance video was not clear enough to identify anyone. The man is in stable condition and expected to recover. No arrest has been announced; the sheriff's office asks anyone with information to come forward.

entries.title: Federal sentence, meth trafficking with guns: Christopher Charles Rogers
body: Christopher Charles Rogers, 51, of Foley, was sentenced to 180 months in prison for a methamphetamine-trafficking conspiracy and possessing guns to further drug trafficking, the U.S. Attorney's Office said Oct. 8.

Prosecutors say he sold meth to an informant at his Foley trailer in early 2025 and was stopped on the Foley Beach Express with about 139 grams after a buying trip to Pensacola; loaded pistols and rifles were found at his home.

entries.title: Federal sentence, felon with a gun: Larry Wooten Jr.
body: Larry Wooten Jr. was sentenced Oct. 5 by Chief U.S. District Judge Jeffrey U. Beaverstock to 37 months for possessing a firearm as a convicted felon.
Prosecutors say Daphne officers responding to a domestic violence report at the Eastern Shore Motel on Jan. 2 found a loaded handgun in his pocket with a serial number someone had tried to file off.

entries.title: Federal sentence, online threat: Robert Davian Grijalva
body: Robert Davian Grijalva, 19, of Loxley, was sentenced Oct. 6 to time served for sending an interstate threat over Instagram, prosecutors said. He had been in custody since 2025.

entries.title: Federal guilty plea, prostitution ring: Felix Albino Lopez-Acahua
body: Felix Albino Lopez-Acahua, of Baldwin County, pleaded guilty in federal court to helping run an interstate prostitution ring and to a federal firearm charge, prosecutors said. They say he and a co-defendant handed out coded business cards at Baldwin construction sites and drove women from Georgia to meet clients.
Sentencing is set for January. The co-defendant, Obeth Quiahua Acahua, pleaded guilty earlier and has been in the county jail since July 17.

entries.title: Fatal crash: motorcyclist killed on AL 59 in Gulf Shores
body: Gulf Shores police say a northbound motorcycle on Alabama 59 struck an SUV turning left at Clubhouse Drive on the night of Sunday, Oct. 18. The rider died at the scene; the SUV driver was not hurt. Police said speed was a factor for the motorcycle. Family members identified the rider to WKRG as Chris Sealy. No charges have been reported.
